text:
Megan Li: Quick Q — prepping the KMS plan for Redwood Private rollout. We need clarity on control-plane vs data-plane CMKs, rotation, and DEK caching. Anyone have a concise pattern we should standardize on?

Raj Patel: TL;DR proposal: separate CMKs for control-plane and data-plane, per-region. Control-plane CMK in management account (customer-owned or our managed?), data-plane CMK per-customer (preferred for isolation) with cross-account grants for dedicated nodes.

Sarah Kim: +1 separate keys. For Private (VPC) customers we usually recommend customer-supplied CMK (BYOK) where possible. If customer can't provide, use a customer-specific key in our shared KMS account with strict key policy.

Alex Gomez: Important: enforce encryption-context at KMS policy level. That prevents accidental decryption of DEKs from another tenant. Example: kms:EncryptionContextEquals { CustomerId: acct-1234 }

Dmitri Ivanov: On rotation: enable automatic rotation only if we have a rewrap job to migrate stored DEKs. Otherwise we need manual rotation + re-encrypt flow. We should never leave cached DEKs valid after rotation without invalidation.

Megan Li: Can someone paste the minimal AWS CLI for GenerateDataKey + re-encrypt for our runbook?

Alex Gomez: Sure — generate a data key (plaintext + ciphertext):

```
aws kms generate-data-key \
  --key-id alias/redwood-private-dataplane-<cust> \
  --key-spec AES_256 \
  --encryption-context CustomerId=acct-1234 \
  --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > dek.cipher
```

Then re-encrypt (rewrap) to new key id: 
```
aws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://dek.cipher \
  --destination-key-id alias/redwood-private-dataplane-<cust>-v2 \
  --encryption-context CustomerId=acct-1234 \
  --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > dek.cipher.v2
```

Raj Patel: Note: use ReEncrypt API (not decrypt+generate) to avoid exposing DEK plaintext in our control plane where possible. If plaintext is needed locally, ensure it never leaves ephemeral memory.

Sarah Kim: For cross-account access we should prefer grants (CreateGrant) rather than broad key policies. Grants can be time-limited and revoked quickly. Also remember to add kms:ViaService conditions if we're calling through other services.

Dmitri Ivanov: DEK cache: set TTL short (e.g., 5 minutes) and add a rotation-wakeup that evicts on successful rewrap. Also publish a rotation event to Ops channel so nodes can proactively re-request DEKs after key rotation.

Megan Li: Audit requirements — what logs do we need to capture and how to tie them to a customer action?

Raj Patel: CloudTrail logs KMS API calls (GenerateDataKey, ReEncrypt, CreateGrant, DisableKey). We should standardize the encryption-context to include CustomerId, DeploymentId, and RequestId so searches are trivial. Keep trails in a central, immutable S3 bucket and mirror to customer's audit location if requested.

Sarah Kim: Add KMS key aliasing convention: alias/redwood/private/<cust-id>/<region> and require that alias in code paths. Prevent direct key ARN hardcoding.

Alex Gomez: RBAC change: we need a new IAM role for private control-plane instances with limited kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:ReEncrypt permissions (resource-scoped), and a separate role for data-plane workers with CreateGrant/UseGrantedPermissions as needed. Update infra IaC to create those roles per-customer.

Dmitri Ivanov: Incident path: if a CMK is suspected compromised — steps: 1) Disable key (schedule a disable if need to preserve rewrap ability), 2) Revoke grants (kms:RevokeGrant), 3) Trigger emergency rewrap to backup key, 4) Rotate keys and force DEK rewrap, 5) Notify customer + runbook. Document RACI.

Megan Li: How do we handle service account key rotation vs CMK rotation?

Sarah Kim: Service account creds are orthogonal. Use KMS to protect long-lived secrets (wrap them). When CMK rotates, rewrap those wrapped secrets (ReEncrypt). For short-lived service tokens prefer STS.

Alex Gomez: Minor ops tip: during rollout enable key-policy kms:EncryptionContextEquals to enforce context. But test in staging first — that can block legacy code paths.

sec-bot: Reminder: there is a scheduled KMS rotation runbook dry-run on 1957654800 UTC. See #eng-sre for invite.

Megan Li: Action items: 1) Raj to draft key policy + grant examples (by EOD), 2) Alex to add CLI snippets to runbook (tomorrow), 3) Dmitri to prototype DEK cache eviction + rotation event (this sprint). Sarah will validate audit/context fields with compliance. I'll follow up with a short doc.

Raj Patel: Will do. I'll include example CreateGrant and minimal key policy with kms:EncryptionContextEquals and cloudtrail note.

Sarah Kim: I'll coordinate with compliance on required fields for encryption-context and retention windows.

Alex Gomez: Ping me if you want help testing rewrap without exposing plaintext. I have a tool that does ReEncrypt-only flow.

Megan Li: Thanks — feel safer having a clear plan. Will post the write-up when Raj shares. :rocket:
